name: Cartograph
tagline: An agent pipeline that maps how a business process runs today, designs an agent-assisted future state, and prices the change with deterministic, evidence-cited arithmetic.
problem: Consulting teams preparing a transformation pitch usually have a client's process taxonomy and an annual report, but little data, and the numbers they present are often generated as prose with self-declared confidence. Cartograph turns that thin input into a per-process blueprint and portfolio value bridge where every claim cites its evidence or is marked as a hypothesis, and every figure can be re-derived from a pinned run manifest.
how: Each case starts as a process from the client taxonomy plus an evidence pack (reports, deliverables, benchmarks) with tiers and publication dates.

Ten specialist agents with structured outputs map the current state, audit workflow debt, score the process, design a future state with agents and an exception model, assess feasibility, model the workforce and estimate value parameters.
A red-team critic challenges claims, and upheld challenges strike evidence before confidence is computed.
Confidence is computed per block from citation coverage and evidence recency, never self-reported by a model.
A reduce stage reconciles the portfolio, counting shared enablers once and ordering prerequisites into waves.
A deterministic Python value engine computes the bridge, run cost, sensitivities and reconciliation, and a read-only React viewer renders the artefacts.
features: Portfolio bridge per currency with base, low and high cases, and an explicit refusal to sum across currencies without an FX rate
Duplication ratio showing gross versus deduplicated released effort when processes claim the same shared capability
Per-prerequisite build cost, run cost by component, reconciliation to a stated baseline, sensitivity table and full assumptions list
Process view with identity, current-state steps, pain points, workflow debt, nine-dimension scorecard, future state, feasibility, implications and value parameters
Evidence chips on every claim that expand in place to show the source item, tier, date and location, with dangling citations flagged
Confidence derivation shown term by term for each block
Provenance view listing every agent, its exact model id and prompt hash, the cache prefix hash and knowledge snapshot id
Replay mode that re-runs every deterministic layer over recorded agent outputs with no model calls, byte-identical each time
Golden eval set with human-written references, rubrics and mutation testing
ai: Ten Claude agents (current_state_cartographer, workflow_debt_auditor, process_assessor, future_state_architect, agent_designer, feasibility_assessor, workforce_modeller, value_estimator, red_team_critic, portfolio_reconciler) each return a structured payload validated against the schema.
Routing sends analysis agents to claude-sonnet-5 and the critic, value estimator and portfolio reconciler to claude-opus-5.
Models supply parameters and judgement only; all arithmetic happens in a Python value package that imports no LLM SDK.
The red-team critic raises objections against specific JSON paths, and upheld objections remove evidence and lower computed confidence.

stack.frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite (read-only run viewer, types generated from the JSON schema)
stack.backend: Python 3.12 pipeline with Pydantic schemas, durable activities and file checkpoints, managed by uv
stack.data: JSON process records, run manifest, value and portfolio artefacts, in-memory evidence store over golden evidence packs
stack.ai: Anthropic API and Claude Agent SDK (claude-sonnet-5, claude-opus-5), deepeval rubrics
stack.deploy: Local; no hosted deployment stated in the repo

screens.title: Portfolio overview
screens.caption: The run header shows the depth tier, schema version, run id and the agents used, followed by the duplication ratio and the shared enablers that several processes claim.

screens.title: Value bridge
screens.caption: One bridge per currency walks from gross benefit through prerequisite, implementation and run cost to net benefit in base, low and high cases. The viewer states why no portfolio total is shown.

screens.title: Prerequisite build cost
screens.caption: Each declared prerequisite is listed with its kind, the wave it is built in, its cost split across claimants and the evidence behind it.

screens.title: Sensitivity
screens.caption: Each value parameter is moved to the low and high end of its band with everything else held, showing net benefit at each end and the swing, so you can see which assumption to check first.

screens.title: Process view
screens.caption: Pick one of the four golden cases to see its identity block: canonical id, taxonomy path, work unit, annual volume, purpose, trigger and output, each with an evidence chip.

screens.title: Current state with evidence
screens.caption: The current-state steps list type, role, systems, elapsed time and effort share. Clicking an evidence chip opens the cited source item inline; uncited steps are marked as hypotheses.

screens.title: Scorecard
screens.caption: The nine-dimension scorecard scored 0 to 5 with a rationale and evidence for each, the two inverted dimensions flagged in the table, and the four nature-of-work axes below.

screens.title: Future state
screens.caption: The redesigned process: designed agents with their tools and data contracts, future steps owned by agents or humans, the exception model and declared assumptions.

screens.title: Value parameters
screens.caption: The parameters the value estimator supplied for this process, with ranges and evidence, plus the shared enablers and prerequisites it depends on.

screens.title: Confidence per block
screens.caption: Confidence is shown as a derivation, not a bare score: citation count, coverage, recency and the product, with agreement marked as not measured.

screens.title: Challenges from the critic
screens.caption: Objections raised by the red-team critic against specific claims, which evidence each one struck, and whether it was upheld.

screens.title: Provenance
screens.caption: Every agent that ran, its exact model id and prompt version hash, and the cache prefix and knowledge snapshot digests that make the run reproducible.

run: uv sync && uv run python scripts/run_pipeline.py --replay && cd frontend && npm install && npm run dev
notes: Ran fully offline. The pipeline was run in its built-in --replay mode, which re-executes the deterministic layers (assembly, validation, citation checks, confidence and value arithmetic, portfolio reconciliation) over agent outputs recorded in evals/recorded/, so no API key was needed. The viewer was started with npm run dev, which collects the replay artefacts, and every screen shows real output for the four golden cases (insurance, financial services, mining, telecommunications). No code was changed. The viewer header reads Workflow Modernization run viewer; the project itself is named cartograph.
